extracted.intended_audience: zoologists, taxonomists, and students identifying and classifying polyzoa (freshwater and brackish species), especially Indian fauna
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological diagnostic criteria and taxonomic keys for identifying Polyzoa (Bryozoa) down to family, genus, and species level, with notes on anatomy, zoarium structure, resting buds, and ecological distribution (focus on Indian freshwater/brackish taxa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Class Polyzoa
rubrics_metrics.description: Small coelomate animals, each individual of which consists of a polyp-like organism or polypide enclosed in a 'house' or zooecium composed partly of living tissues. The mouth is surrounded by a circle of ciliated tentacles that can be retracted within the zooecium; the alimentary canal... is Y-shaped and consists of oesophagus, stomach, and intestine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these gross body-plan characters (polypide in a zooecium, retractile tentacular crown, Y-shaped gut) as primary diagnostic features for assigning organisms to Polyzoa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subclass distinction: Entoprocta vs Ectoprocta
rubrics_metrics.description: Entoprocta: the anus as well as the mouth is enclosed in the circle of tentacles and the zooecium is not very distinctly separated from the polypide. Ectoprocta: the anus is outside the circle of tentacles and the zooecium can always be distinguished from the polypide; all species form permanent communities by budding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position of the anus relative to the tentacular crown and the degree of separation of the zooecium from the polypide are key characters to separate Entoprocta and Ectoprocta (also solitary vs colonial tendencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order Gymnolæmata diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ectoproctous polyzoa the polypides of which have no epistome; the zooecia are in nearly all cases distinctly separated from one another by transverse perforated plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an epistome plus zooecia separated by transverse perforated plates indicates Gymnolæmata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suborder Cheilostomata (within Gymnolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia provided with a 'lip' or lid hinged to the posterior margin of the orifice; lid closes automatically outside the zooecium or in a special chamber (the 'peristome') and is pushed open by the tentacles. Many zooecia are flattened; some modified to vibracula and avicularia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a hinged operculum/lip and often flattened zooecia (plus specialized avicularia/vibracula) identifies Cheilostomata; mostly marine but some estuarine/brackish occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suborder Ctenostomata (within Gymnolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia provided with a collar-like membrane pleated vertically which closes together above the polypide inside the zooecium when retracted; it expands into a ring before tentacle extrusion. Zooecia usually tubular, sometimes flattened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pleated collar (collar-like membrane) that inverts/expands during retraction/extrusion is diagnostic of ctenostomes; majority marine but includes freshwater lineages (Paludicellina).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suborder Cyclostomata (within Gymnolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia provided neither with a lip nor with a collar-like membrane. They are tubular and usually have circular orifices. Cyclostomata are exclusively marine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of both lip and collar, tubular zooecia with circular orifices, and marine habitat separate cyclostomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order Phylactolæmata diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ectoproctous polyzoa whose polypides have a leaf-shaped epistome projecting upwards and forwards within the tentacular circle and between the mouth and anus. Zooecia are not distinct from one another; in dendritic forms zoarium divided by chitinous partitions. Phylactolæmata are freshwater species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of an epistome and indistinct zooecial separations (with freshwater habitat) indicate Phylactolæmata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division characters within Ctenostomata: Alcyonellea
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia arise directly from one another in a fleshy or gelatinous mass. The polypide has no gizzard. Species essentially marine (few brackish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth as a gelatinous mass and absence of gizzard delimit Alcyonellea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division characters within Ctenostomata: Stolonifera
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia arise from expansions in a delicate creeping rhizome or root-like structure (stolon); order irregular. As a rule there is no gizzard. Species marine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connection via stolons/rhizome and lack of gizzard identify Stolonifera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division characters within Ctenostomata: Vesicularina
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia grow directly from a tubular stem usually free and vertical; arrangement alternate, spiral or irregular. There is a stout gizzard with internal chitinous projections tightly compressed when polypide retracted. Species essentially marine (few brackish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical tubular stem habit plus stout gizzard with internal chitinous projections distinguishes Vesicularina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division characters within Ctenostomata: Paludicellina (nov.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia arranged in a regular cruciform manner and arise either directly one from another or with tubular processes; if the polypide has a gizzard it does not bear internal chitinous projections. Most species confined to fresh water (some brackish/sea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cruciform arrangement of zooecia and freshwater habitat (and gizzard without internal chitinous teeth when present) mark Paludicellina; includes all true freshwater ctenostomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Paludicellidae (family-level diagnostic characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium recumbent or erect, typically of zooecia arising in cruciform formation or joined by tubules; zooecia tubular with terminal or subterminal angulate/subangulate orifice appearing as four flaps/valves; polypide with elongate slender alimentary canal and long oesophagus; tentacles often 8 (Paludicella may have 16); resting buds (hibernacula) present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use zoarium formation (cruciform/tubular), characteristic orifice shape (four flaps), polypide gut morphology, and presence of resting buds to diagnose Paludicellidae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genera key within Paludicellidae (Pottsiella, Victorella, Paludicella)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Orifice terminal; main axis vertical; zooecia separated by tubules. A: base not swollen; no adventitious buds = Pottsiella. B: base swollen; adventitious buds near tip = Victorella. II. Orifice subterminal on dorsal surface; main axis horizontal; buds not produced at tip = Paludicella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genera by orifice position (terminal vs subterminal), axis orientation (vertical vs horizontal), base-swelling and production of adventitious terminal buds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Paludicella diagnostic notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium linear/occasionally branched, recumbent or partly vertical; zooecia tubular with upturned tip bearing orifice; parietal muscles always present; polypide lacks gizzard; alimentary canal specialized (cardiac stomach form); two funiculi connect stomach to endocyst; tentacles may be 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of gizzard, presence of parietal muscles, two funiculi, and characteristic orifice position separate Paludicella from Victorella and Pottsiella. Collar pleats are delicate/transparent—may be hard to see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Victorella diagnostic notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium of erect/semi-erect tubular zooecia joined at base cruciformly; adventitious buds/tubules produced profusely around terminal region, often giving tangled mass; no parietal muscles; polypide with 8 slender tentacles and a gizzard (oesophageal sac) bearing a thin internal membrane; single funiculus; resting buds flattened or zooecium-like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of an evident gizzard, single funiculus, lack of parietal muscles and prolific adventitious terminal budding are key to Victorella identification; can be more brackish/marine in occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species: Victorella bengalensis distinctive characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Mature zoarium resembles a thick fur of elongate erect slender tubules; base often an irregular membrane; young zooecia ovoid with stout quadrate orificial tubule projecting; adventitious buds frequently produced near tip, sometimes connected by long tubules; polypide with gizzard base surrounded by a strong circular muscle; resting buds flat with marginal cylindrical projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use overall 'fur-like' zoarium, yellowish tint, adventitious terminal buds, and resting-bud morphology to distinguish V. bengalensis from similar species (e.g., Bowerbankia caudata). Ecology: common in brackish pools in Ganges delta; feeds largely on diatoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Hislopiidae diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium recumbent often forming uniform flat layer; zooecia flattened, adherent, orifice dorsal either surrounded by chitinous rim or at tip of erect chitinous tubule; no parietal muscles; polypide with an ample gizzard uniformly lined with chitinous layer which does not close on retraction; resting bud not produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flat, adherent zooecia with dorsal chitinous rim and a distinctive uniformly chitin-lined gizzard separate Hislopiidae from Paludicellidae and Victorellidae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Hislopia diagnostic and anatomical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium with a main straight axis and forward-pointing lateral branches (may compact into a flat area); zooecia flat with orifice rim; polypide with 12–20 tentacles; funiculus rudimentary or absent. Gizzard unique: thick-walled tubular portion communicating with a spherical chitin-lined chamber; ring of long powerful cilia around passage to stomach; gizzard wall with outer muscular and inner glandular layers; gizzard contains green cysts (ingested organisms) acting as food reservoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complex gizzard structure (tubular upper part + chitin-lined spherical chamber + ciliary ring) and presence of green cysts are diagnostic of Hislopia; be wary of superficial resemblance to cheilostomes caused by chitinous orificial rim—this is convergence, not true relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of resting buds (hibernacula) in identification and life-history notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Resting buds are masses of cells at the base of zooecia, gorged with food, covered with horny coat; in Paludicellidae ('hibernacula') they may be produced at the approach of summer in India and germinate in November/December. Resting buds vary in shape (spindle-shaped in Paludicella; flattened or zooecium-like in Victorella) and can persist across seasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence, morphology, timing, and germination behavior of resting buds are useful taxonomic and ecological characters (seasonality may differ by region). Rename 'hibernacula' to 'resting buds' where seasonal timing differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary of key morphological terms used for identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions supplied for terms such as 'swim-ring' (ring of polygonal air-spaces around statoblast), 'ventral surface' (surface nearest anus of zooecium/polypide; of statoblast the surface by which attached to funiculus), 'zoarium' (whole body of zooecia in organic connection), 'zooecium' (parts constituting a case/house for the polypide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these precise definitions when observing specimens to avoid misinterpretation of structures (e.g., ventral vs dorsal surfaces, zoarium vs individual zooecia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautionary guidance on convergent morphology and misclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: Some genera (e.g., Hislopia) have superficial resemblances to cheilostomes (e.g., chitinous rim suggesting peristome) when examined in preserved/dried material; live examination reveals ctenostome characters. Misidentifications (e.g., Paludicella vs Victorella) can arise from juvenile/adult stages or from poor preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer examination of living specimens and internal anatomy (gizzard presence/structure, parietal muscles, funiculus number, tentacle count, adventitious budding) to avoid errors; check for seasonally produced resting buds that may alter appearance.
